name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
headline: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has an electronic record in its public clinics, but its only privacy law has not been in force since 2003.

access.summary: No law gives patients an enforceable right to their record: the Privacy Act 2003 and Freedom of Information Act 2003 were never brought into force. A hospital policy promises a free review and a paid copy, but no portal exists.
detail: Both the Privacy Act 2003 and the Freedom of Information Act 2003 start only on a day set by ministerial order. The UWI Data Protection Office says no order for the Privacy Act had been made as of February 2025. In 2019 iWitness News reported the FOI Act had still not taken effect.
Even if commenced, the Privacy Act covers only public authorities. It would let a person ask a public body to correct personal information, including medical history.

The Ministry of Health's patients' guide for Milton Cato Memorial Hospital says patients may review their medical records free and get a copy at the stipulated cost. The fee and any deadline were not found.

No patient portal was found. The score sits in the 15 to 35 band for no enforceable right, level with Grenada and Saint Lucia (uncommenced law, no portal); the hospital policy is not enforceable, so it adds nothing.

control.summary: With no privacy law in force, patients have no legal say over who sees their health data. Records sit in a single ministry system used across public clinics, with no opt-out or patient-visible access log found.
detail: The Ministry of Health says its Health Information System (SVGHIS) aims to give every resident an electronic identification code and record, and to link all major service areas of the ministry.
No consent rule, opt-out, granular choice or access log for SVGHIS was found. The Privacy Act 2003 would limit how public bodies use personal data, but it is not in force.
The hospital patients' guide promises privacy and confidentiality of records, except where reporting is required by law. It is a policy, not an enforceable right.
In June 2026 the government said a unique ID system will let ministries share citizen information securely. The score sits in the 20 to 35 band for default sharing with no choice.

privacy.summary: There is no data protection law in force and no regulator: the 2003 Privacy Act and its Privacy Commissioner exist only on paper. The US State Department said in September 2026 that no specific data protection law has been adopted.
detail: The Privacy Act 2003 would create a Privacy Commissioner with powers to investigate complaints against public bodies and report to Parliament. It covers only the public sector and was never commenced, so no Commissioner exists (UWI Data Protection Office).
The State Department's 2026 Investment Climate Statement says the government passed the Privacy Act in 2003 but has not adopted any specific data protection legislation.
The 1979 Constitution protects the privacy of the home and protects against search of the person without consent. No breach notification duty, health data law or health-sector enforcement was found.
The score sits below the 45 to 66 general-law band because no general law is in force.

commercial.summary: No law limits the sale of health data, its use in marketing, or data brokers. The only privacy statute is not in force and would cover public bodies, not private firms.
detail: The Privacy Act 2003 applies to public authorities such as ministries, statutory bodies and local authorities. Private clinics, insurers, pharmacies and app makers are outside it, and it is not in force anyway.
The State Department said in September 2026 that no specific data protection legislation has been adopted.
No rules on health apps, data brokers or de-identified data sales were found, and no enforcement action was found.

journey.summary: The ministry's Health Information System holds electronic records at 36 to 45 public facilities, but the main hospital's records were on paper when PAHO last reported (undated story). Current coverage of hospital, lab and pharmacy links was not verified.
detail: An undated Ministry of Health page says SVGHIS is used daily at 36 facilities, with working modules for electronic health records, maternal and child health, clinician order entry, supply chain, HIV and human resources. Laboratory and public health modules are listed as planned.
An undated PAHO story says SVGHIS was 85 percent implemented at 45 facilities. It said Milton Cato Memorial Hospital records were paper-based, with a project to scan over 30,000 files into SVGHIS.
No e-prescription system or national insurance claims system was found. A new hospital at Arnos Vale is being built, and the government said in January 2026 that Milton Cato will close once it opens.
Public health surveillance draws on 50 clinics; PAHO reported national integrated surveillance guidelines in draft in June 2026.

clinical.summary: A clinician at a public facility on SVGHIS can open the patient's electronic record and enter orders. The main hospital's history sat in paper files in an undated PAHO report, and private practices are not known to be linked.
detail: The ministry says SVGHIS runs clinician order entry and electronic health records at the facilities using it, and aims to network hospitals and district clinics.

PAHO said (undated story) that Milton Cato's records since 1984 were on paper. The scanning project aimed to let several clinicians see a patient's history at once and encourage use of SVGHIS. Whether the scanning was finished was not verified.
No link between private doctors and SVGHIS, and no emergency access rule, was found.

research.summary: No law governs research use of health data or requires ethics approval for trials, according to the 2012 national pharmaceutical profile. The main hospital's patient guide does let patients refuse to take part in research.
detail: The 2012 Pharmaceutical Country Profile, published by the Ministry of Health with PAHO, says no law requires authorisation of clinical trials, ethics committee approval, or trial registration. No later trials law was found.
The uncommenced Privacy Act 2003 would allow public bodies to use personal data for research if it is not published in an identifiable form.
The Milton Cato patients' guide says patients may refuse to take part in research and join only after a full explanation.
No opt-out or register of research uses was found. Score: base 40, plus 3 for the hospital consent route.

ai.summary: No AI law, strategy, regulator or medical device rule for clinical AI was found. A September 2026 benchmark found no AI-specific framework in any of 13 Caribbean countries, this one included.
detail: A June 2026 compliance tracker says there is no AI Act, no national AI strategy in force and no AI regulator. It says the previous government promised an AI policy in September 2025, then lost the November 2025 election.
Cullen International's September 2026 benchmark of 13 Caribbean countries, including this one, found none has an AI-specific regulatory framework.
No medical device regulator was found. The 2012 pharmaceutical profile names the Pharmacy Act 2002 as the medicines law. The absence of any rule was not confirmed with the ministry.
